expected_differences: Demo Roastery and its D initial replace the Lab’s fictional business identity.
The roster shows two recorded members—demo (You, Owner) and Priya Nair (Manager)—with their stored handles, join dates and available avatar media.
The member initial is an appropriate fallback; no replacement portrait is invented.
Invitations are explicitly unavailable, so there is correctly no Invite action or fabricated invited state.
keep: The 200px graphite rail, restrained TapMart mark, selected Business item and 32px desktop content gutter.
Mineral canvas #F4F3EF, white information surface and restrained divider rules, without shadows or floating management cards.
The 36/40px application title, strong section heading, readable operational copy and ink-colored roster roles.
The compact 576px reading column, aligned role values, circular member avatars and muted handle/date metadata.
The concrete permission descriptions, plain invitation limitation and both Settings return controls.
review.readiness_note: Sign off for the captured 1440×900 viewport. The screen exposes the recorded membership, role capabilities and navigation coherently; click-through behavior and server-enforced permissions still require functional testing.
review.why: The supplied Lab capture is Business Home, not a Team fixture, so this is a system-level comparison. Production preserves its shell, mineral surfaces, typography hierarchy and restrained color use while correctly simplifying the composition for management. The two-person count matches the two visible rows; names, provenance and roles are clearly separated. Permission descriptions distinguish the owner’s financial authority from the manager and member roles. The invitation notice states the actual limitation rather than presenting unsupported controls. Everything fits without clipping or crowding. No source-to-commitment offset, financial anchor or large media assembly is needed here, and none has been added decoratively.
review.verdict: Frame Shift was faithfully transferred to Team at desktop size, with the visible membership, permissions and navigation intact and no release-blocking drift.
